From Gautam Buddha to Jain Tirthankaras, India has had the privilege of serving as the land of spiritual traditions. One such wonder located in the remote Himalayas is Gurudwara Hemkund Sahib. The gurudwara is one of the most revered sites for Sikhism followers, and the pilgrimage to the site is considered deeply significant.Amid Uttarakhandâs Garhwal Himalayas, the gurudwara is located at an altitude of 4,632 metres and is surrounded by seven Himalayan peaks. The beauty of the site is enhanced by a glacial lake in the middle of the peaks. Currently, the journey to the site is strenuous, as pilgrims must undertake a steep trek of almost 19 kilometres. However, the ropeway project is underway, which will make the holy site more accessible to everyone, especially the elderly.The Spiritual Legacy of Guru Gobind SinghThe significance of the gurudwara is rooted in its association with the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh. Finally, Sri Kalgidhar Chamatkar by Bhai Vir Singh documented the search for the sacred site and its historical significance.The site was rediscovered in 1934 when retired army granthi Sant Sohan Singh trekked to it after being inspired by Bhai Vir Singhâs writings. They also installed a handwritten copy of the Guru Granth Sahib to consecrate the holy tapasthan.How to visitThe difficult 19-kilometre trek starts from Govindghat, which is approximately 280 kilometres from Rishikesh by road. From Govindghat, the 13-kilometre trek route is relatively well maintained and passes through the village of Ghangaria. After that, a further 6-kilometre stone path leads to Hemkund Sahib. There are no accommodation facilities at the site, so pilgrims must plan their return journey carefully and follow the local authoritiesâ recommended trekking timings.Due to heavy snowfall around the gurudwara, it remains inaccessible for most of the year. Check the official website for the annual opening dates before visiting.By AirJolly Grant Airport in Dehradun is the nearest airport for travellers heading towards Hemkund Sahib.
